paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: This figure illustrates the maximum activation values across transformer layers for a baseline model, as indicated by the title "Massive Activation of baseline." The X-axis is labeled "Layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The Y-axis is labeled "Max Activation Value" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200. Four lines are displayed. The blue dashed line labeled "attn_output" remains near 0 from layer 0 through approximately layer 20, then rises sharply to around 600 by layer 23. The orange dotted line labeled "attn_residual" stays near 0 until approximately layer 5, where it rises steeply to around 1400, then continues increasing gradually to approximately 1550 by layer 15, remains relatively stable until around layer 20, and then drops sharply back toward 600 near layer 23. The green dash-dot line labeled "ffn_output" remains near 0 until layer 5, where it spikes sharply to approximately 1400, then drops back down close to 0 around layer 7, remains near 0 until approximately layer 13, spikes again to around 500 near layer 14, drops back to near 0 around layer 15, stays low until layer 20, and then rises sharply to approximately 600 by layer 23. The red solid line labeled "ffn_residual" stays near 0 from layer 0 to approximately layer 5, rises steeply to about 1500 around layer 6, remains relatively stable at approximately 1500–1570 from layer 6 through layer 20, and then drops sharply to around 400 near layer 23. A legend is positioned in the center-right area of the plot, listing all four lines with their corresponding colors and styles.

The red solid line represents "ffn_residual"; it stays near 0 from layer 0 to approximately layer 5, then rises steeply to about 1400, continues increasing to approximately 1500 by layer 7, remains relatively flat around 1500–1550 through layer 20, and then drops sharply to approximately 400 at layer 23.
